appraisal_events.evidence: C'était mon article qui avait enfin paru! ... l'ensemble de l'article se trouvait élevé aux nues par une foule ... [je voyais] la répétition de mon nom ... briller sur eux, en une aurore qui me remplissait de plus de force et de joie triomphante.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's long-awaited article finally appears in Le Figaro, and he savors an imagined mass readership that elevates the piece; the passage narrates this as a triumphant personal elevation, the dominant movement of the passage.

appraisal_events.evidence: Dès qu'elle me l'eut donnée, ma mère avait forcé Françoise à rebrousser chemin et l'avait entraînée dehors, effarouchée, offensée et surprise ... le sourire noirâtre et gluant d'une pitié transcendante et d'une ironie philosophique ... Pour ne pas se sentir méprisée, elle nous méprisait.
appraisal_events.explanation: Françoise is abruptly turned out of the narrator's room, a privilege she considers her due, and the narration mockingly exposes her wounded self-love and the defensive contempt she manufactures to cover the humiliation.

status_effects.explanation: The publication of his article is narrated as a personal triumph, filling him with pride and a sense of collective admiration.
She is physically removed from the narrator's room, a space she normally considers hers to enter and stay in at will, marking a local boundary closing against her.
The narration gently ridicules her wounded pride and the self-protective contempt she adopts to avoid feeling despised, locally diminishing her in the telling.
